title: Vizcom
subtitle: 3D Brand World & Motion
overview: I worked with Outland on a 3D brand film and a series of short 2D animations for Vizcom’s new identity.
The main film explores a working design studio, with branded tools, screens and objects throughout. The shorter pieces focus on the chair, app icon and graphic patches.

hero.alt: Vizcom brand world inside a sunlit design studio
hero.posterAlt: Vizcom brand world inside a sunlit design studio
hero.title: Vizcom dynamic 3D brand world mockup

caption: Brand-world animation · 32 seconds

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Bring Outland’s new identity for Vizcom into a space that feels like a designer’s studio. The 3D film was the main piece, with shorter 2D animations exploring individual parts of the identity.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I built the studio around a workbench, moving from wide views of the room into close-ups of stationery, screens and materials. For the 2D pieces, I focused on simple changes: a chair moving from sketch to colour, a shifting app icon, and patches moving through repeating type.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I created the 3D environment, materials, lighting and camera animation, and rendered the film and stills. I also animated the 2D pieces, working from Outland’s identity and creative direction.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The finished film and stills show the identity across a complete studio, from the room itself to the objects on the desk. The shorter animations give the chair, app icon and graphic details their own moments in landscape, square and portrait formats.

title: ValkaAI
subtitle: 3D Glass Prism Logo Animation
overview: I worked with Less and Better on a 3D animation of the ValkaAI logo.
The mirrored butterfly becomes a glass prism, with blue and orange light and images of AI personas passing through its surfaces.

hero.alt: ValkaAI mirrored-butterfly logo rendered as a refractive glass prism
hero.posterAlt: ValkaAI mirrored-butterfly logo rendered as a refractive glass prism
hero.title: ValkaAI 3D glass-prism logo animation

caption: ValkaAI · Glass prism logo animation

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Animate the mirrored butterfly from Less and Better’s identity. The sequence needed to show the shape of the mark and make room for ValkaAI’s persona imagery.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I gave the logo depth and a refractive glass material. Moving light and imagery through the prism let me explore its symmetry, edges and reflections.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I handled the art direction, 3D work and motion graphics for the animation, working with Dominik Smuchar and Petr Skovajsa from Less and Better.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The finished loop shows the logo as a glass object, with the persona imagery visible through it. Blue and orange light carry the identity’s colours through the sequence.

title: The Mag Wrap 2025
subtitle: 3D Motion & Show Graphics
overview: For The Mag Wrap 2025, I explored how a set of 3D shapes and materials could carry a rap show’s graphics.
The package includes an intro, looping backgrounds, show IDs and reusable on-screen graphics.

hero.alt: The Mag Wrap judges displayed above red team labels in a dark 3D arena

caption: The Mag Wrap 2025 · Motion package

approach.label: Brief / Why I did it
paragraphs: I wanted to develop a visual approach that could work across a whole show: from an opening sequence to smaller graphics for names, judges and standings.

approach.label: Process / Tools & thinking process
paragraphs: I used Blender and Houdini for 3D, Nuke and After Effects for compositing and motion, and DaVinci Resolve for the edit.
I reused shapes, materials and movements across the package, adapting the compositions and timing to each format.

outcome.label: My role / What I made
paragraphs: I developed the art direction, 3D animation and motion graphics. That included the intro, show IDs, loops and templates for recurring on-screen information.

outcome.label: Result / What I learned
paragraphs: The finished package uses the same visual elements at different scales. Building the pieces together helped me see which ideas worked as a full-screen sequence and which stayed clear in a small graphic.

title: Barbour
subtitle: Icons in Quilting · FOOH Campaign
overview: I directed the CGI and VFX for Barbour’s Icons in Quilting campaign with Monopo London.
Quilted fabric spreads through footage of London, New York, Seoul and Shanghai, followed by plants and countryside details.

hero.alt: CGI ferns growing along a city pavement in Barbour’s Icons in Quilting campaign

caption: Barbour · Icons in Quilting campaign

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Bring Barbour’s quilted fabric into city scenes for the Icons in Quilting campaign. The films combine real locations with oversized fabric and elements of the British countryside.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: We tracked the camera footage and reconstructed the parts of each location that the CGI needed to interact with. Cloth animation and procedural plants were built in Blender and Houdini, then composited into the filmed scenes.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I led the CGI production and worked on animation, VFX and Houdini simulation. Josef Talač and David Hájek contributed 3D, VFX, animation and modelling, alongside Monopo’s creative and production team.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The campaign includes four city films and two department-store sequences. Each uses the same quilting idea in a different location.
About 407k views were recorded across the four city Reels on Barbour’s Instagram on 23 September 2026. This is a combined count for those posts.

title: Victoria’s Secret
subtitle: VSX Sports Bra · CGI Animation
overview: I worked with TMRZV Studio on a CGI product film for the VSX Sports Bra.
The sequence moves from individual yarn loops and the woven VSX logo to close views of the finished fabric and bra.

hero.alt: Lime knit loops forming fabric and the VSX logo before a close view of the sports bra

caption: VSX Sports Bra · Knit and fabric detail

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Show the construction of the VSX Sports Bra in a short product film. The animation needed to connect the small details of the knit with the shape of the finished product.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I built the knit and weave simulations in Houdini, from interlocking yarn loops to the raised VSX logo. In Blender, I refined the materials, lighting and product views.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I created the 3D product animation, materials and lighting, along with the Houdini simulations. TMRZV Studio handled creative direction, sound and compositing.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The film brings the fabric details and product views into one sequence. The accompanying breakdowns show how the yarn loops and woven logo were built.

title: Chainer
subtitle: Jewellery in 3D
overview: I used jewellery as a starting point for a series of 3D scenes, experimenting with landscapes, light and reflective materials.
The project grew to include stills, animation, sound and a website, all built around the same objects.

hero.alt: A silver necklace above a sculpted display stand, blue landscape and orange sun

caption: Chainer · Jewellery animation

approach.label: Brief / Why I did it
paragraphs: I wanted to explore the setting around a small object. The jewellery needed to remain the focus, while the surroundings gave each image its own atmosphere.

approach.label: Process / Tools & thinking process
paragraphs: I started with the object and its material, then built the lighting and setting around it.
I adjusted reflections, contrast and camera position to keep the jewellery visible within the larger scene, then carried those choices into the animation and website.

outcome.label: My role / What I made
paragraphs: I developed the art direction, 3D scenes and animation, worked on the sound, and designed and built the website.

outcome.label: Result / What I learned
paragraphs: Working across stills, animation and web made me pay attention to how the scenes connected. A consistent use of light and materials helped the different formats feel like parts of the same project.

title: Vojta Zizka
subtitle: Automated Patreon "Thank You" & Market Charts
overview: I built two tools for Vojta Zizka that turn changing data into finished video graphics.
Patreon supporter lists become animated credits. Market data becomes branded charts, ready for the edit.

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: I wanted to make recurring graphics easier to update. Supporter names and market data change between episodes, while the design of the credits and charts stays consistent.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I connected the data to reusable graphics. A Patreon CSV feeds an After Effects script, while a web app fetches market data and turns it into charts.

chapters.title: Automated Patreon "Thank You"
chapters.description: An After Effects script reads a Patreon CSV export and generates animated supporter credits. I designed the layout and animation around the list of names.

media.alt: Vojta Zizka podcast end screen with animated Patreon supporter credits

chapters.caption: CSV to animated supporter credits

chapters.title: Automated Market Charts
chapters.description: A web app fetches market data and generates seven-day charts in the show’s visual style. It exports the graphics as still images or animations.

media.alt: Branded market charts beneath a Vojta Zizka video conversation

chapters.caption: Automated charts in the finished video

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I built both tools, designed the graphics and created the animation. The work combined scripting with the practical requirements of a video edit.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: Both tools turn updated data into graphics for the edit. ProductionBot’s project description gives these estimates for preparation time per video:

title: Gusto
subtitle: UI Design Showreel
overview: I worked with Chris Wilcock from Outpost Studio on a showreel for their new UI design for Gusto.
The film moves between interface details and warm 3D device scenes, with playful transitions connecting the two.

hero.alt: Gusto UI design showreel combining animated layouts with warm desktop, laptop and phone scenes

caption: Gusto · UI design showreel

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Show the new Gusto UI as a connected experience. The reel needed to make room for the design’s themes, modules and page layouts, as well as the smaller interactions that give it personality.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I moved between close views of the interface and wider device scenes. Colour changes, stacking layouts and cursor movements carry the UI sequences, while warm light and everyday desk details give the film a more human feel.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I created the 2D and 3D motion for the showreel, working with Chris from Outpost. My focus was on bringing their UI design into motion and connecting the screen sequences with the device scenes.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The finished showreel brings the new UI together in one film. The landscape and portrait sequences also let individual moments stand on their own, from changing themes to a close-up of the site on a phone.

title: Shelby
subtitle: Custom Device & Merch Mockups
overview: Ashfall Studio asked me to create custom mockups for their Shelby brand case study.
The scenes present the identity on screens and merchandise, from a MacBook in a sunlit workspace to pins, badges, bottles and clothing.

hero.alt: Shelby website on a MacBook in a sunlit workspace with wood surfaces and a perforated wall

caption: Shelby · Custom MacBook mockup

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Show Ashfall’s Shelby identity on devices and physical objects. The mockups needed to make room for the website’s animation as well as the materials and printed details of the merchandise.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I placed the devices against wood and a perforated backdrop, using directional sunlight to frame the screens. For the merchandise, I used simple colour fields and close views of the shapes, surfaces and graphics.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I created the 3D device and merchandise mockups. Martin Ehrlich led creative direction at Ashfall, and Dominik Budimir contributed motion design.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The set gives Ashfall still and animated views for the Shelby case study. It ranges from the website on devices to close-ups of a rotating pin, an event badge, a bottle and clothing.

title: Rounds

The scenes move from a clubhouse overlooking the course to phones, a watch and branded merchandise.

hero.alt: Rounds clubhouse interior with curved seating, branded objects and a view across the golf course

caption: Rounds · Clubhouse brand world

paragraphs: Build a setting for Outland’s Rounds identity, showing the app on devices and the brand on physical objects. The clubhouse and golf course provide the surroundings for those details.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I used warm wood, soft seating and a view onto the course to connect the interiors with the landscape. Closer shots focus on screens, printed graphics and metal surfaces.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I created the 3D environments and custom mockups. Jordan Jenkins and Evan Place led the identity and creative direction at Outland, with Matko Mijić contributing 2D motion design.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The animated scenes show the Rounds identity across a clubhouse, a golf course, devices and merchandise. Wide views establish the setting; closer views show the app, a flask, a keychain and a poster.

title: Trezor
subtitle: Hardware Wallet Product Animation
overview: I worked with Yiskra on 3D product animations for Trezor’s online store.
The sequences show the hardware wallet in black, green and orange, moving between its overall shape and details of the screen and textured back.

hero.alt: Green Trezor hardware wallet rotating against a light background

caption: Trezor · Product animation

approach.label: Brief
paragraphs: Create product-page animations that show the hardware wallet clearly in each colour. The lighting and motion needed to fit Trezor’s existing visual style.

approach.label: Process
paragraphs: I used gradual rotations and changes in lighting to reveal the profile, screen and textured back. Reflections describe the surfaces against a light background.

outcome.label: My role
paragraphs: I handled the 3D work, animation and lighting, with Tomas Gnosis Snop managing the project at Yiskra.

outcome.label: Result
paragraphs: The finished set presents all three colours with consistent framing, lighting and movement. Close views show the surface details, while wider shots follow the shape of the wallet.
